articles.title: Fantasy Football Week 11 RB Report: Another fumble makes D'Andre Swift tough to trust, plus more backfield splits
articles.summary: We go over some key backfield splits from Week 11 and what it means for fantasy football going forward.
articles.body:
Let's take a second to appreciate the backup running back and the importance of having that insurance on your bench. Emmett Johnson drew another start in place of the injured Kenneth Walker III on Sunday. For the third time in four weeks, the rookie back went for 22+ fantasy points on a hefty 23 carries for 105 yards and a score, plus four catches for 38 yards. Most of that damage was done well before the game clock wound down in the fourth quarter.

If you're a Walker manager who was smart enough to add Johnson back after Week 8, nice work. If you were like me (in one league) and didn't grab Johnson to replace Walker, well … it's been a rough watch the past month or so.

In this piece, we talk a lot about backfield splits and depth running backs, specifically, in an attempt to inform you for future weeks. Let's see what the highlights and box scores show us that we can use for fantasy football going into Week 12 and the Thanksgiving week slate.

It was an ugly week in general for the Bears offense in a spot we thought could produce points, considering the team had an implied total around 30. Instead, we got inconsistency, particularly in the run game despite the return of Kyle Monangai. He had missed the past five games due to turf toe and a thumb injury. This was also an elite matchup for running backs; New Orleans entered Week 11 allowing the sixth-most rushing yards per game and sixth-most rushing TDs this season.

While Swift got to an OK floor for fantasy purposes because of a short TD catch, he could be back in the doghouse after another lost fumble, his third of the season. As a result, we saw carries for fourth-string RB Salvon Ahmed, with Roschon Johnson leaving the game early due to an ankle injury. Monangai also wasn't his usual efficient self, though we're willing to give him a pass coming back after a long absence.

Let's talk about Swift first. In games following a Swift fumble, Swift maintained a heavy workload with 22 touches in Week 3 and 13 in Week 5 (no Caleb Williams). So Swift shouldn't lose his role, but he also hasn't been all that impressive. He doesn't have a carry longer than 15 yards since Week 1 and doesn't have a catch that went for more than 13 yards since Week 2. Ben Johnson could opt to lean more on Monangai, but he and Swift have had a relatively even split of the carries when both are healthy, with Swift being more of a threat in the passing game. Ahmed also didn't look all that bad and could leech a few touches.

The next two weeks aren't ideal, either. The Bears get the Lions on Thanksgiving on the road and the Jaguars in Week 13, two of the worst matchups for RBs in fantasy. It will be tough to count on both Swift and Monangai as anything more than flex options in the short term, and after that we could see the latter take on more work if he can stay healthy. The matchups soften a bit in a key stretch from Weeks 14-16.

Maybe it was the Panthers defense but the Ravens offense looks revived with Jacoby Brissett under center. At least for fantasy purposes. Baltimore scored 33 points and had over 400 yards of offense Sunday in the narrow loss to Carolina . For real life, it was brutal. For fantasy managers, it was a sigh of relief for those with Henry and Zay Flowers.

But we're here to talk about the backfield specifically, where Henry got back to work with his highest total on the ground since Week 5, when he went for over 100 yards rushing. He now has four total TDs in the past three games and a useful nine catches in the past two. A lost fumble put a minor dent in his final total as well.

Despite getting back on track the past two weeks, at least from a fantasy points perspective, there's still cause for concern for Henry managers. And it's in the form of Hill.

The backup RB put together another strong outing, nearly reaching 100 total yards on just 10 touches with a 19-yard TD before halftime. Hill also had a 36-yard long rush in the game that resulted in a fumble just before scoring. All in all, he continues to showcase big-play ability. He entered the game averaging 6.8 yards per carry and had 11.5 per against the Panthers. That's going to keep Hill involved.

Looking ahead, how Baltimore performs down the stretch could play a factor in how this backfield looks for fantasy managers. With six straight losses, sitting at 4-7, the Ravens aren't entirely out of the playoff picture. They still have four division games left (two against the Steelers). But a few more losses could sink Baltimore and that could lead to less work for Henry and more for Hill. We recommended Hill in the early waiver piece going into Week 12 .

Henry is still an RB2 for fantasy but there's also the Week 13 bye — not ideal. Hill has shown he can be an RB3/flex with upside. If you have Henry, you need Hill on your bench. If you're looking for a potential league-winner late in the season, Hill has that upside if the chips fall right.

Kamara can't keep getting away with this, can he?

Last week, it was a tilting five touches for 14 total yards and two scores. This week, it's just TWO yards on two touches, but another touchdown. Seven other carries went to various skill position players and QB Tyler Shough. But at least it was a decent showing by Etienne in his second game back after being placed on injured reserve after Week 3.

It wasn't a dominant performance by Etienne but it was good enough for his managers to trust him back in their lineups. Most of his 76 yards came on a 46-yard run, but that's fine; we wanted to see Etienne get back to making big plays, and that was his biggest of the 2026 season. The volume was also a great sign with Audric Estimé a healthy scratch for Week 11; the backfield was all Etienne's.

The larger issue is the Saints offense. It's not performing up to par, like the boat races and shootouts we saw in flashes last season after Shough took over. The O-line isn't great and Shough has regressed a bit. The rest of the fantasy schedule lines up well for points (at CIN, vs. GB, at CAR), which is a plus. But we need to see some progress from Kellen Moore's group overall in order to have faith in Etienne as an RB2.

The back has that potential but he'll need 15-20 touches and a few big plays mixed in. Etienne is going to lose snaps to Kamara and New Orleans likes using the vet in the red zone. This game has us putting Etienne back in the RB2/3 range, while Kamara is only a risky, TD-dependent flex.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Week 11 Booms and Busts: We can all be thankful for the Dallas Cowboys offense
articles.summary: Fantasy football analyst Scott Pianowski examines the winners and losers of Sunday's Week 11 action.
articles.body:
In the chaotic and erratic world of fantasy football, it sure is nice when we can find some weekly constants. There won't be many. But take this to the bank in 2026: the Cowboys have a fun offense. And it's needed to offset a lousy defense.

The Cowboys played to their reputation in Sunday's wild 51-30 victory over Tennessee. The Pokes assembled six straight touchdown drives to start the game, doing anything they wanted. Dak Prescott had as many total touchdowns as incomplete passes (five of each). Dallas never punted, collecting 33 first downs and 480 yards of offense.

Prescott was the QB1 in fantasy last week, and he's poised to hold that post again. As we go to press, he's almost 11 points ahead of the field. He's thrown for 300-plus yards in three straight games, and he's racked up nine touchdown passes the last two weeks.

As usual, Prescott kept the target tree especially narrow. CeeDee Lamb (11-132-1) and George Pickens (7-102-1) drew 22 of Prescott's 33 targets; no one else saw more than three. It was a buzzkill if you needed to gamble on Ryan Flournoy (1-11-1, one target) but the primary guys were eating.

The Dallas backfield has been streamlined all year, too. Javonte Williams turned 21 touches into 91 total yards and a couple of scores, one by land and one by air. He's not having a special year by efficiency, barely over four yards per rush. But with the consistent usage and the goal-line equity (12 touchdowns now) he holds on a plus offense, Williams has easily been a profit at his ADP.

The Titans were the shakier side of this game, as Tennessee started slowly and was never in danger of winning. But eventually the Titans put some drives together and mostly came home for fantasy, even as most of it felt garbage-timey.

Cam Ward ultimately threw for a couple of scores and punched in a one-yard run, justifying his love as a one-week rental. One of the TD passes was to Carnell Tate (2-58-1), a fluky play where Dallas thought Tate was down by contact but he wisely kept the play alive and turned it into a 59-yard score. Tony Pollard was oddly ignored as a receiver — it's almost like the Titans missed the tape of last week's Dallas-San Francisco game — but he still rolled to 110 rushing yards. It was a good week to remember some Titans.

And that's a common thread when we're talking Cowboys — stack the opponents. The over is now 8-3 in Dallas games this year, despite the totals being in the 50s more often than not. This week's number was set at 54.5 and the Pokes almost got over it by themselves.

The remaining Dallas schedule isn't necessarily ideal, but again we need to consider the strengths and weaknesses of this club. The Cowboys host Philadelphia on Thanksgiving, then it's a pesky two-week stretch (at Seattle in Week 13, bye week in Week 14).

Dallas gets the Rams, Jaguars and Giants in the fantasy playoffs, Weeks 15-17. Those matchups could go either way, I suppose. The Rams have been a tough team to figure all year, and they've been injury-riddled. The Jaguars can look dominant one week and mediocre the next, but that's the NFL for you. Any given Sunday . . . or Thursday . . . or Wednesday . . . or Black Friday.

But maybe we shouldn't look that far ahead. Let's get to Dallas on Thursday and watch this offense do its thing. Hopefully the Eagles don't forget to punch back. And let's keep those Dallas carnival tickets ready for December, too.

The other fun game from the early window came in Carolina, where the Panthers escaped with a 35-33 win over the Ravens. All of the NFC South teams have been a mess at home this year (collectively 5-17), so you take the wins where they come. It was a nice validation game from a couple of offenses that have teased us — occasionally productive, but lacking consistency.

Mind you, there are no knocks on Chuba Hubbard (27-120-2); he's smashing his ADP as the prime guy in Carolina's backfield. He didn't draw a target Sunday, but with rushing stats like that, no one cares. Bryce Young had one of his better games (8.2 YPA, two touchdown passes), and he looked to Tetairoa McMillan liberally (6-71-1, nine targets). It's still hard to trust Jalen Coker, but he came out of his slump somewhat, with a 4-47-0 line on seven opportunities. Baby steps.

The harshest reality of the Carolina offense is the upcoming schedule: Tampa Bay and Minnesota. Thankfully, the opponents get more reasonable after that, though the Panthers also draw Seattle in Week 17.

On the Baltimore side, Jacoby Brissett did what he usually does — sustain offense, keep the game competitive, ultimately lose. This is the same music that played in Arizona. Brissett chucked for 276 yards and got 7.5 YPA, mostly centering on uncoverable Zay Flowers (8-97-0, 11 targets). It was frustrating to see Mark Andrews draw just three targets, as the overall passing tree was narrower than expected.

Derrick Henry (13-94-1) looked spry and also had four short catches, though he was dinged up late in the game. Justice Hill (10 touches, 96 total yards, one score) has been involved more than expected. Hill probably isn't a fantasy start next week with all 32 teams in play, but depth always matters.

Like the Panthers, the Ravens aren't heading into a fun part of the schedule. Here is how Baltimore ends the fantasy season: at Texans, bye, Buccaneers, at Steelers, Browns, at Bengals, at Steelers. We'll take it week by week.

It was a slow-developing Polaroid, but ultimately all the Detroit offensive angles came in against the nasty Tampa Bay defense. Jahmyr Gibbs (118 total yards) had two touchdowns, Amon-Ra St. Brown (5-37-1) and Jameson Williams (4-93-1) both spiked and Sam LaPorta had a useful 3-62-0 line (tight end is so gross this year). Jared Goff remains one of the most underrated QBs around, and we always love him indoors and at home. That's the Thanksgiving assignment, when the Lions host Ben Johnson and the Bears. Get your pies and popcorn ready.

Maybe the Chiefs are becoming fun again, not that a boat race over the Cardinals tells us much. Patrick Mahomes was hardly touched, rolling to an easy 324 passing yards and three scores. Emmett Johnson is such an impressive player, 23-105-1 almost feels like merely a par. He also caught four passes for 38 yards. Travis Kelce (6-74-2) had his first multi-spike game in three years and Josh Downs (4-59-0) and Rashee Rice (6-53-0) were at least heard from. Kansas City at Buffalo looks like a blast on Thanksgiving night.

Consider this a placeholder for Jonah Coleman, who's trying to win you a fantasy game all by himself. The Broncos aren't finished with the Raiders yet, but as we go to print, Coleman is sitting on 20 carries, 100 yards and three rushing touchdowns. He's fully taken the backfield over — J.K. Dobbins has just one carry. And the less the Broncos have to throw, the better.

Ashton Jeanty is doing his share on the other side, running better than usual and crushing in the passing game, as expected. Because of the receiving work, Jeanty never is a risk of being game-scripted off the field. The Raiders get Cleveland next week, while Denver heads to Pittsburgh.

Even with Kendre Miller cut and Audric Estimé out, the New Orleans backfield couldn't come in for us. Travis Etienne Jr. was given ample opportunity — he had one 46-yard run but otherwise made just 30 yards on 13 attempts. He was a zero in the passing game. Alvin Kamara vultured a short touchdown catch but only had two touches; CJ Donaldson (4-12-0) was the main pass-catching back. Lovely, a three-headed monster.

The Saints also continued to be a first-quarter mess, going scoreless to open at Chicago. Somehow New Orleans has just nine points in the first quarter all year.

You never give back wins, but the Bears basically played with their food in the 21-13 win over the Saints. Chicago finished with 18 first downs and 311 yards, under expectations. Caleb Williams didn't give anyone more than four targets and the Bears only threw the ball 23 times; it hurt that the Saints didn't fight back much. Even the backfield was a cast of thousands, toggling between D'Andre Swift (13-51-0, though he had a TD catch), Kyle Monangai (8-18-0) and Salvon Ahmed (6-33-0). We fully expect a make-up performance Thursday in Detroit.

If Aaron Rodgers wanted to retire tomorrow, I doubt anyone would mind. Rodgers managed just 5.2 YPA in a 19-16 loss to the Eagles, a Philadelphia team that finally snapped a seven-game losing streak. The DK Metcalf ejection didn't help, not that Metcalf (1-2-0, four targets) was doing anything. Both of the Pittsburgh backs were bottled up, and the surprise receiving star was Max Hurleman (6-61-1), who didn't have a career catch before Sunday. Pittsburgh hosts Denver next week, a game I am not looking forward to.

articles.title: Fantasy Football: George Kittle, 49ers offense win the day versus Vikings' league-best defense
articles.summary: Fantasy football analyst Chris Allen examines Sunday's major storylines in Week 11.
articles.body:
I've been married for almost 20 years, and you'd think I'd be used to things changing in an instant. I mean, I've had plenty of practice. Just last Friday, my evening plans switched from nothing (my default choice) to my wife inviting a couple over for board games, to her going to play cards with her sisters. It did turn out to be a quiet night for me. But it reminded me that in our house, a plan is, well, more of a suggestion.

I should've remembered that lesson as we headed into Sunday. From the kickoff to the early games, Week 11 reminded me how quickly things can flip in just a week. Honestly, I came away with more questions than answers. Let's dig into the storylines on some of the things that changed the most.

Before SNF, nobody wanted their QB to face the Vikings. The only passer to throw for multiple TDs was Jordan Love back in Week 1. Jared Goff in Week 8 was the first to complete over 70% of his passes against Minnesota's defense. And for TEs specifically, Keleki Latu was the sole player at his position to score against DC Brian Flores' unit.

Brock Purdy and George Kittle raised the bar in Mexico City.

Of course, the Vikings came in with their usual approach. Purdy saw five or more rushes on 73.3% of his passing attempts. That didn't matter. One, the blitzes only got home once. And two, only one incompletion was the result. Eight of his 10 completed passes turned into a first down or a score. Kittle was the primary fantasy beneficiary of Minnesota opting to treat Purdy like every other QB. But the rest of the receiver corps chipped in, too.

Target Rate: 26.9% (Evans), 15.4% (Samuel), 15.4% (Allen)

The "Unc Bowl" was in full effect for HC Kyle Shanahan. None of his aged WRs ran more than 50% of the snaps. But when they were out there, you knew where the ball was going. But the Vikings' secondary couldn't stop them. All four of the 30-plus-year-old pass-catchers were responsible for at least one explosive play. Only Christian McCaffrey got left out in the cold (he still found his way to the end zone ). Minnesota's defense looked mortal for the first time all season.

But the state of the offense is a bigger issue.

Passing Success Rate: 43.6% (Week 11), 47.1% (Week 10)

After a confidence-building week against the Packers with Kirk Cousins fresh off the trade, everything came to a halt against San Francisco. Aaron Jones Sr. and Jordan Mason combined for a 35.3% rushing success rate on early downs, leaving Cousins with 8.6 yards to go in obvious passing situations. Justin Jefferson lost a fumble on a play where he (maybe?) would've scored if he hadn't changed directions. Cousins threw a pick-six . That's two possessions that could've tightened up the score. But as the Vikings were trying to catch up, an old fantasy option returned.

T.J. Hockenson came back to a part-time role after missing Week 10 with wrist and chest injuries. However, despite running the fewest routes of any of the starting pass-catchers, only Tai Felton had more targets. Hockenson should be in starting TE slots moving forward. But for Felton, I'd be more wary. The team opted not to place Jordan Addison on injured reserve , expressing optimism that he can be out on the field sooner than the IR designation. So, unless you're in dire need of a receiver, Hockenson should be the only addition from the Vikings off waivers as we head into Week 12.

Let's review Sunday's expectations for the Bears. The Saints' run defense came into the game allowing the 10th-most yards per game on the ground over their last six contests. Quinshon Judkins was the only starting RB to face New Orleans and exit with single-digit PPR points. HC Ben Johnson not only had Kyle Monangai returning from injury, but also the bye to plan.

Even in the first half, the results were concerning.

The Bears' approach to play-calling to start the game was simple: let's establish the run. D'Andre Swift touched the ball on the first four plays. Five of the nine plays on their opening drive were runs. Chicago finished the day with an -8.8% PROE (a season-low mark). Said another way, the volume was there. But Johnson split the pie up a few ways.

Swift: 48.0% (Early-Down Touch Rate), 37.0% (Route Share), 53.8%(RZ Snap Rate)

Swift and Monangai swapped series throughout most of the contest. Luckily for gamers rostering Swift, it was No. 4 who was on the field for Chicago's first TD drive after CJ Donaldson fumbled on their side of the field. Swift got the lone touch from inside the 10-yard line and converted for the score. But therein lies the problem. The combination of a healthy Ben Johnson running game and (theoretically) poor resistance from New Orleans should've garnered more production from anyone carrying the rock. Instead, we got the opposite.

Credit to the Saints' defensive line. They met the trio of Bears' rushers at or behind the LoS on 51.9% of their attempts. Monangai wasn't known for being the shiftiest of runners (0.0% forced missed tackle rate), but averaging 1.9 yards after contact didn't help. Swift took all of the short-yardage totes and only came out with one conversion on three attempts. And to make matters worse, Salvon Ahmed mixed in on early downs, siphoning yards away from both.

I could use the Bears' quick turnaround to face the Lions on Thursday to explain Ahmed's usage. However, season-lows in efficiency, leading to Caleb Williams' third-down environment getting more chaotic (fourth-highest average distance to convert), aren't just about the rotation. And after watching the Lions keep the Bucs' ground game in check, the Bears will need to adjust their run game in order to stay in the race for the top spot in the NFC North.

I understood Pittsburgh coming out flat against the Bengals in primetime last week. Don't get me wrong, I was surprised in the moment. But I've seen these games between division rivals before. I didn't expect to see the output continue a week later.

Aaron Rodgers' scramble to close out the first quarter was the longest running play for the Steelers on Sunday. If you're rostering Jaylen Warren, apologies in advance. After enjoying the backfield to himself for a stretch, maintaining the starter role and putting up three RB1 finishes, Warren was becoming a staple of fantasy rosters. However, everything's taken a step back.

Rushing Success Rate: 54.6% (Weeks 1-8), 28.6% (Week 10), 22.2% (Week 11)

Adj. Yards After Contact per Att.: 4.97, 2.14, 2.67

Pittsburgh's biggest play-calling shift was in how often Rodgers dropped back to pass. After having a negative PROE for three straight games, the Steelers were up to +6.3% (fourth-highest on the season). Accordingly, Warren carried the ball just nine times (second-fewest in '26). Philadelphia held him to zero yards before contact on two-thirds of his carries and stuffed him on a third. But that's OK. With more passing, Warren's involvement as a receiver should've kept his fantasy value afloat. However, his QB was also still in a slump.

Pressure-to-Sack Ratio: 62.5%, Season-high

The worst part is that the Eagles largely left Rodgers alone. They blitzed him just once. And yet, Rodgers still hit his season-high of five sacks. But I can't blame him. DK Metcalf decided that fighting with the defense was more important than catching the ball. And sure, Germie Bernard earned 10 targets. But again, six of them were on throws of five air yards or less. Rodgers didn't regularly look for him on intermediate or deep throws until the second half.

The knee-jerk reaction from gamers might be to start Bernard in Week 12. Metcalf might incur a suspension . Rodgers has been more efficient targeting Bernard over Metcalf in multiple games. However, with the Broncos and Texans on their upcoming schedule, I'd keep everybody in black and gold on your bench.

My largest concern with Fernando Mendoza starting during this stretch of games for the Raiders was the absence of Brock Bowers. I realize neither he nor HC Klint Kubiak could plan for an injury. But the chasm between Bowers and the rest of the pass-catchers would put anyone in a tough spot. And having to face Denver, coming off its bye, without his de facto WR1 would be a challenge. However, I didn't give enough credence to the idea that Kubiak could prepare his QB to do more with less.

To be clear, it wasn't all pretty. The Raiders punted on their first three drives. Mendoza ended the first quarter with just one more completed pass than sacks taken. It wasn't until the half was winding down that Mendoza started to get into the flow. But if there were concerns about whether or not Kubiak was giving Mendoza answers to the defense's questions, the rookie alleviated some of them.

EPA per Dropback: -0.02 (Week 11), -0.18 (Week 10)

Instead of forcing the ball to the middle of the field without his best receiver, Mendoza looked to the perimeter. It was the ideal adjustment given the strengths of the skill players he had on hand. Plus, he's pretty good at it. Mendoza averaged 0.68 EPA per dropback with a 55.6% completion rate on boundary throws. But Mendoza wasn't just aggressive — he was decisive, averaging more throws under 2.6 seconds. Oh, I guess I buried the lede there. All of his TD throws were to the perimeter. And at least one of his target-earners shouldn't be a surprise.

Unfortunately, not much changed for Ashton Jeanty as a runner. Six of his 11 carries came with a defender in the backfield. Denver held him to three or fewer yards on 54.5% of his attempts. But Jeanty came into the game behind only Christian McCaffrey in YPRR and was fifth in YAC per reception. If there was going to be a way to get Mendoza comfortable with the offense, using Jeanty as a receiver was the right call. But there's one more pass-catcher who should be on our radar.

Jack Bech's routes and targets have gone up in three straight weeks. He led the team in looks after Bowers left in Week 10 and was just one shy of Tre Tucker's total in Denver. But with receiving aDOTs of 9.3 and 8.1, Bech won't have the same volatility as a downfield option like Tucker. So even with Bowers likely to return, Bech should be a speculative add if you have the bench space.

New York Hands Jacksonville a Giant Upset

Talk about narratives changing in a week. Jacksonville made multiple additions to the defense before the trade deadline, needed the full four quarters to get by Tennessee but, on paper, looked like one of the favorites to get to the Super Bowl.

And then the Giants reminded them there are no easy matchups in the NFL.

To be fair, the signs were there for the Jaguars to face some problems on offense. Starting LT Anton Harrison tore his ACL in Week 5, and C Robert Hainsey missed this game with a knee sprain. Minor injuries to RT Cole Van Lanen and RG Ezra Cleveland only complicated the situation further. Coincidentally, the G-Men were second to the Vikings in blitz rate and ninth in sack rate over their last six games. The outcome was one of Lawrence's worst outings this season.

Completion Percentage Over Expected: -2.1%, 3rd-lowest

Jacksonville's issue wasn't just that Lawrence's protection kept breaking down, but how fast things deteriorated. DC Dennard Wilson had his unit getting to Lawrence in 2.5 seconds or faster on 12 of his dropbacks. That's four more than his previous season-high. Accordingly, Lawrence's average time to throw skyrocketed to 3.3 seconds. He started taking more shots downfield (12.1 passing aDOT). Of course, the Giants mounting a multi-score lead by the end of the first half prompted the aggression. But New York reducing them to a one-dimensional offense was the larger issue.

Rushing Success Rate (on early downs): 27.3%, Season-low

Distance to the Sticks (on third downs): 10.8, Season-high

Bhayshul Tuten entered the game with foot/ankle injuries, missed time earlier in the game and then left early with a limp . Meanwhile, Chris Rodriguez Jr. ran into a stacked box on every single one of his early-down rushing attempts. Without a running game, Jacksonville turned into a dropback passing unit.

Let's assume Tuten misses Week 12. Jacksonville has its rematch against the Titans. Rodriguez is healthy. He should be at or near the top of your waiver priority. But I'd be wary about expecting similar target totals for Jakobi Meyers (10) and Josh Cameron (7). Lawrence just attempted more than 45 passes for the first time since Week 7 of last season. Unless you think the Titans can do the same, the offense should go back to its balanced ways in Week 12.

articles.title: David Sánchez se rinde a Alcaraz y Márquez: "Si está sano, es muy complicado que no bata todos los récords de la historia"
articles.standfirst: El presentador de Despierta San Francisco ha aprovechado su tiempo de opinión en La Tribu para rendir homenaje a los dos deportistas españoles y destacar el futuro del tenista
articles.summary: El presentador de Despierta San Francisco ha aprovechado su tiempo de opinión en La Tribu para rendir homenaje a los dos deportistas españoles y destacar el futuro del tenista
articles.body: David Sánchez ha arrancado este lunes su habitual 'picotazo' en La Tribu de Radio MARCA con un homenaje a dos de los grandes protagonistas del deporte español: Marc Márquez y Carlos Alcaraz. El periodista ha querido destacar los éxitos de ambos deportistas durante el fin de semana, poniendo especial énfasis en el potencial del tenista murciano para seguir haciendo historia. "Valga el picotazo de hoy por la mañana para homenajear a las dos cabras que nos deja este fin de semana, una en el motor y la otra en las pistas de tenis", ha comenzado David Sánchez, utilizando el término 'GOAT' para referirse a los dos deportistas. Marc Márquez, por encima de Valentino Rossi El periodista ha dedicado sus primeras palabras al piloto español, al que ha situado entre los mejores de todos los tiempos tras su nuevo éxito en MotoGP. "Otro nuevo mundial, uno más de MotoGP, suma 10 y se convierte directamente en uno de los más grandes de la historia del motor", ha señalado. Además, David Sánchez no ha dudado en compararlo con uno de sus grandes rivales históricos: "Una auténtica leyendaza, muy por encima ya de su archienemigo Valentino Rossi". Alcaraz y un futuro sin límites Sin embargo, el otro gran protagonista de su editorial ha sido Carlos Alcaraz. Sánchez ha destacado la trayectoria del murciano y ha recordado las palabras de Alexander Zverev al finalizar su encuentro: "Carlos, tienes 23 años, si hoy te retirases ya serías una leyenda del mundo del tenis". "Espectacular lo que está haciendo el murciano. Si no se cansa de este deporte, que no tiene pinta, Carlitos Alcaraz tiene un techo espectacular", ha asegurado el periodista, convencido de que todavía le quedan muchos éxitos por delante. Por último, David Sánchez ha puesto el foco en la importancia del estado físico del tenista para seguir ampliando su palmarés. "Le queda mucho por ganar y ahora además es consciente que se tiene que cuidar para competir sano", ha explicado antes de cerrar con una contundente reflexión: "Porque si está sano, es muy complicado que este tipo no bata todos los récords de la historia de este deporte".

articles.title: Pepe Brasín compara a Marc Márquez con Michael Jordan y Nadal: "Son unos psicópatas"
articles.standfirst: El colaborador de 'La Tribu' de Radio MARCA destaca la mentalidad competitiva del piloto español y le sitúa a la altura de las grandes leyendas de la historia del deporte
articles.summary: El colaborador de 'La Tribu' de Radio MARCA destaca la mentalidad competitiva del piloto español y le sitúa a la altura de las grandes leyendas de la historia del deporte
articles.body: Marc Márquez pertenece a una categoría reservada para unos pocos elegidos. Su trayectoria, marcada por los éxitos, las lesiones, las caídas y una capacidad de superación extraordinaria, le ha situado entre los grandes nombres de la historia del deporte. Una dimensión que va mucho más allá de sus resultados sobre la moto y que tiene en su mentalidad competitiva uno de sus principales argumentos. Sobre esa personalidad del piloto español habló Pepe Brasín en 'La Tribu' de Radio MARCA, donde estableció una comparación con algunas de las mayores leyendas del deporte mundial. "Cuando hablamos de Marc Márquez, hay que hablar de Michael Jordan, de Novak Djokovic, de Rafa Nadal, de Tiger Woods o de Max Verstappen", señaló el colaborador, que quiso poner el foco en una característica que comparten todos ellos: una competitividad llevada al extremo. "Lo primero que te viene a la cabeza es que son unos psicópatas, que son unos seres competitivos hasta el extremo", explicó Brasín para describir la mentalidad de estos deportistas. Una exigencia que, en su opinión, permite entender la dimensión de Márquez y su capacidad para mantenerse en la élite incluso cuando las circunstancias no han sido favorables. El colaborador de 'La Tribu' repasó los diferentes escenarios a los que ha tenido que enfrentarse el piloto de Cervera a lo largo de su carrera: desde sus épocas doradas hasta los momentos más complicados, marcados por las lesiones, la soledad y la incertidumbre sobre su futuro. También hizo referencia a los cambios de contexto deportivo, a las diferencias de rendimiento entre las motos y a los periodos en los que Márquez ha tenido que competir sin disponer del material más competitivo de la parrilla. Sin embargo, Brasín encontró un denominador común en todas esas etapas: su hambre de victoria. "En todas las circunstancias, el punto común es que Marc Márquez es un competidor fiero, extremo, que lo da todo por ganar, todo, todo el rato", sentenció. Una reflexión que sitúa al ocho veces campeón del mundo en el selecto grupo de deportistas cuya mentalidad competitiva les permite marcar una época.

articles.title: El Hyatlón crece en 2027: más sedes, aplicación de la IA y de nuevo final en Zaragoza
articles.standfirst: El nuevo circuito constará de 8 o 9 sedes, adoptando un nuevo sistema de puntuación
articles.summary: El nuevo circuito constará de 8 o 9 sedes, adoptando un nuevo sistema de puntuación
articles.body: La primera edición del Hyatlón Ambar Tour vivirá este fin de semana su gran final en Zaragoza tras su tres citas previas en Madrid, La Nucía y Gran Canaria. El éxito del circuito , tanto a nivel de participación como de organización, queda plasmado en los planes de futuro para 2027: constará de 8 o 9 sedes, adoptando un nuevo sistema de puntuación. Además, el hybrid racing implementará Inteligencia Artificial para el arbitraje. José Hidalgo, presidente de la Federación Española de Triatlón, confirmó que la capital aragonesa repitará en 2027 como sede de la gran final gracias a el apoyo de Turismo de Aragón, la Feria de Zaragoza, el Ayuntamiento de Zaragoza, el Gobierno de Aragón y sus excelentes prestaciones organizativas. En 2027, la competición arrancará en Sevilla en el mes de enero y recorrerá plazas como Madrid, Sabadell, Tenerife, además de perfilar sedes en la zona norte (La Rioja o Santander) y el sur con Marbella, además del Levante (Alicante o Murcia) y Extremadura (Badajoz o Cáceres). El funcionamiento del circuito importará el modelo del Mundial de Motociclismo o las World Triathlon Series. Los deportistas de todas las categorías irán sumando puntos en las pruebas regulares, pero será en la Gran Final zaragozana donde se reparta la mayor puntuación y se decidan los campeones absolutos. Jose Hidalgo confirmó que España lidera mundialmente el desarrollo de esta disciplina, recibiendo consultas semanales de otros países para replicar este modelo pionero. Esta expansión tiene el objetivo de que el hyatlón sea olímpico. El presidente apuntó directamente a los Juegos de Brisbane 2032, aprovechando que el hybrid racing tiene una gran implantación en Australia y que el país anfitrión puede incluir hasta cuatro deportes nuevos de forma oficial. Para estar a la altura de estas ambiciones, el Hyatlón liderará también la innovación técnica. Para acabar con la percepción subjetiva de los jueces voluntarios y garantizar la máxima justicia a los atletas de élite, la FETRI, junto con uno de sus colaboradores, está haciendo pruebas para implantar un sistema de Inteligencia Artificial. Mediante sensores en el brazo y la pierna de los deportistas, el sistema determinará con exactitud si ejercicios como los Wall Balls, el Remo o los Burpees se ejecutan correctamente, una tecnología que se perfecciona cada día gracias al análisis de miles de pruebas. La FETRI ha reafirmado su voluntad de sumar fuerzas con el sector privado, desde ayuntamientos hasta grandes operadores como Hyrox o Deka, para crear una gran comunidad unida. Asimismo, la Federación trabaja en una formación que cuente con el reconocimiento y la validación oficial del Estado, garantizando titulaciones independientes de marcas comerciales o universidades.

articles.summary: Discover the implications of Dylan Larkin's transfer from the Detroit Red Wings to the Montreal Canadiens in this trade update, exploring the benefits for both teams and what his arrival means for Montreal's NHL ambitions.
articles.body: The Montreal Canadiens made a splash with a blockbuster NHL trade Sunday night, November 22, acquiring Dylan Larkin from the Detroit Red Wings. The deal also includes two draft picks heading to Montreal, while Detroit receives several players and substantial draft capital.Larkin's departure ends a difficult period involving his trade request, removal as Detroit's captain, and suspension. His arrival gives Montreal an experienced center as the Canadiens look to strengthen their lineup and compete at a higher level.Montreal Canadiens acquire Dylan Larkin from Detroit Red WingsThe Montreal Canadiens surrendered a considerable collection of assets to complete the deal. According to the official announcement, Detroit received:Forward Kirby Dach.Goaltender Samuel Montembeault.Forward prospect Michael Hage.A conditional first-round pick in the 2027 NHL Draft.A second-round pick in the 2027 NHL Draft.A fourth-round pick in the 2028 NHL Draft.A conditional first-round pick in the 2029 NHL Draft.In return, Montreal received Larkin, Detroit's second-round selection in 2028 and third-round selection in 2027.The two first-round selections carry conditions. If Montreal's 2027 pick falls within the top 10 after the draft lottery, the Canadiens can retain it and transfer their 2028 first-round selection instead. A similar condition applies to the 2029 pick, which could shift to 2030 if it becomes a top-10 selection.Why did the Detroit Red Wings move on from Dylan Larkin?Larkin’s exit comes after months of speculation about his future in Detroit. The 30-year-old center initially requested a trade during the offseason, with the situation eventually becoming public.The Red Wings also removed him from the captaincy, a position he had held since January 2021. After returning from an upper-body injury and recording six points in 10 games, Larkin informed Detroit on October 29 that he no longer intended to play for the organization.Larkin gives the Montreal Canadiens a center with lots of NHL experience and a proven scoring touch. His scoring touch, leadership pedigree, and ability to play in different situations could help stabilize the forward group.Before his ban, he had two goals and four assists in 10 appearances in the 2026-27 season. His last production also shows he is a reliable scorer.Larkin is signed through the 2028-29 season, with five years left on the eight-year, $69.6 million deal he agreed to with Detroit in March 2023. Montreal gets a longer-term option at center on his contract, not a short-term rental.For Detroit, this is a different direction. Kirby Dach is a forward ready to make the NHL, and Samuel Montembeault has NHL goaltending experience. Michael Hage could be a key prospect, particularly after he had scored 26 points in 13 games for the University of Michigan in the 2026-27 season at the time of the trade.Finally, the blockbuster deal is two different approaches. Montreal is doubling down on a well-established hub to shore up its existing core, while Detroit has added younger talent and assets with an eye toward the future.The biggest question now is whether Dylan Larkin can help the Montreal Canadiens convert their big investment into sustained NHL success.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: The Louisiana Ragin’ Cajuns faced an early deficit against No. 18/22 USC and were unable to overcome the Trojans’ hot start, falling 82-56 on Sunday
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES ( KLFY ) – The Louisiana Ragin' Cajuns faced an early deficit against No. 18/22 USC and were unable to overcome the Trojans' hot start, falling 82-56 on Sunday at the Galen Center.

USC (6-0) scored the game's first 10 points and built a 17-1 advantage before Louisiana (1-4) began to find its rhythm. The Ragin' Cajuns trimmed the deficit to 17-6 following a layup by Dani Pounds, but the Trojans maintained control and carried a 42-27 lead into halftime.

Louisiana continued to battle in the second half, but USC used its size and offensive efficiency to maintain its advantage. The Trojans shot 48.8 percent from the field, including 9 of 19 from 3-point range, and connected on 31 of 40 attempts at the free-throw line.

Jamyron Keller led Louisiana with 13 points, including three 3-pointers, while Deion Ware added a season-high 10 points off the bench. De'Vion Lavergne contributed eight points, four assists and three steals for the Ragin' Cajuns, and Dani Pounds finished with five points and a team-high seven rebounds.

USC was paced by Alijah Arenas and Rodney Rice, who scored 18 points apiece. Darius Ratliff added 17 points, while Adonis Ratliff chipped in 14 points and eight rebounds.

The Ragin' Cajuns dressed nine players for the contest, with Todd Jones Jr. seeing his first action of the season after missing Louisiana's first four games. Jones finished with five points and five rebounds in 11 minutes before fouling out with 4:01 remaining.

Mikhail Dulkay added six points and six rebounds for Louisiana, which finished 20-for-54 (37.0 percent) from the floor and 7-for-22 (31.8 percent) from behind the 3-point line.

Louisiana will return home Tuesday to host Louisiana Christian as part of a men's and women's basketball doubleheader at the Cajundome. Tipoff for the men's contest is scheduled for 7:30 p.m.

articles.title: 5 takeaways from the Bears' stifling win over the Saints
articles.summary: The Bears took care of business by handling the Saints at Soldier Field. Here are our takeaways from the victory.
articles.body:
The second half of the 2026 season got underway for the Chicago Bears Sunday when they welcomed the New Orleans Saints to rainy Soldier Field, much like their meeting last year. And just like that game from 2025, the Bears followed a similar gameplan to get a win. They managed the game enough on offense to keep New Orleans out of reach and put on an excellent defensive display with sacks and turnovers galore to get the 21-13 win.

The Bears kicked things off with an opening scoring drive, taking a 3-0 lead. From there, quarterback Caleb Williams scored a pair of touchdowns, including a shovel pass to D'Andre Swift and a quick throw to Colston Loveland to go up 16-0. Once again, it looked like the Bears were set to cruise to a big win. But instead, they put on cruise control and allowed the Saints to slowly catch up.

New Orleans cut the deficit to 16-10 going into halftime with a touchdown and a field goal in the second quarter. But the Bears wouldn't allow the Saints to get much closer. A few big defensive plays, most notably a safety sack by Montez Sweat and a failed fourth-down conversion deep in Bears territory, prevented the Saints from coming back. Chicago gets their fifth win in a row to improve to 8-2 on the season, their best 10-game start in 20 years.

It was another win that didn't look pretty for much of the day but still keeps the Bears atop the increasingly competitive NFC North ahead of a pivotal Thanksgiving matchup against the Detroit Lions . Here were our takeaways from the win:

1. The Bears purposely took their foot off the gas

Coming out of the bye week, many Bears fans were looking past the Saints in order to get to the Detroit Lions on Thanksgiving, a monumental matchup when it comes to jockeying for the division lead and a playoff berth. Ben Johnson talked earlier in the week about keeping the focus on the here and now, but perhaps his actions spoke louder than his words.

When the Bears went back up by two scores in the third quarter, it felt like Johnson took his foot off the gas while thinking ahead to Thursday, like he did against the Atlanta Falcons. Over the final four possessions, there were just four dropbacks by Williams, including penalties. The Bears seemed content trying to run the clock out and do enough to get the win.

This isn't to excuse the offense failing to capitalize on more opportunities. The Bears should have been far more effective when it came to running the ball and taking care of the ball. Those errors won't be good enough to overcome against the Lions. But with the short week approaching and the Saints' issues across their entire team, it's plausible that the Bears dialed their gameplan back once they built a big enough lead.

What more even needs to be said at this point? As Mike Tomlin said on Football Night in America, Simmons is an apex predator who is at the top of the food chain. He eats offensive linemen like Galactus, the Devourer of Worlds, showing he has a never-ending hunger for quarterbacks and running backs.

Simmons tied a career high with three sacks on Sunday, something he hasn't accomplished in over five years. He also had three QB hits and four total tackles. Simmons lined up all over the defensive line, getting two at defensive tackle and another at defensive end. At nine sacks across the season, he's on pace for a career year and continues to elevate everyone around him. We're witnessing something special along Chicago's defensive line, and Simmons is only getting better the more comfortable and familiar he gets with his teammates.

3. Zavion Thomas finally has a role in the offense

There wasn't a whole lot to be excited about when it comes to the Bears offense, but rookie wide receiver Zavion Thomas stood out for what he was able to do with his touches. For the last few games, Thomas had been getting ingratiated into the gameplan, though he became somewhat of a pariah during his last outing for a foolish personal foul penalty. This week, however, it was time for his coming out party.

Thomas had two catches for 56 yards, both coming in spectacular fashion. Thomas' first grab was on a beautiful flag route in which he burst past his defender, where Williams found him in stride. The second came on a stellar comeback play where he barely beat the defender to the ball for a first-down conversion, as Williams had pressure bearing down on him. He also took an end-around handoff for 30 yards to set up the Bears' second touchdown of the day.

It feels as if we're starting to see the shift from Williams and the offense depending on Kalif Raymond to giving Thomas more opportunities. Johnson has shown his penchant for slowly working in rookie receivers, and Thomas is starting to check all the boxes when it comes to getting the details correct. He's already come a long way in a short period of time, and this could be the start of a big finish to the season for him.

4. Clark Phillips deserves more playing time

Sometimes there are players that always seem to flash when they get on the field. Especially when those opportunities to be on the field are few and far between. Clark Phillips has become one of those players for me. He rarely sees the field as one of the reserve cornerbacks, but he always seems to make a play when he gets an opportunity to shine.

Phillips saw more action than in any other game this season due to Kyler Gordon's shoulder injury. He totaled four tackles (one for loss), a sack, a pass deflection, and a forced fumble, earning a game ball for his efforts. His four tackles were the most in over two years.

Of course, Phillips wasn't perfect, as his clear miss on Saints quarterback Tyler Shough's long conversion is an issue, but Phillips is a dog who gets after the ball carrier. He deserves more snaps at cornerback, whether that's on the inside or the outside. And he could be needed against a team like Detroit, who can present problems with Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams.

5. D'Andre Swift's fumbles are officially concerning

I am not yet pushing the panic button when it comes to D'Andre Swift's fumbling issues, but it's been placed on the desk with the glass case still covering it. Swift coughed up his third fumble of the year on Sunday, tying his single-season high for his career. Fortunately, the Saints were too inept to convert the turnover into points, but this is becoming a bit of a problem.

The last time Swift fumbled was in Week 4 against the New York Jets, which turned into points for the opponent. Swift sat the rest of the game and gave way to Kyle Monangai, which played a role in his toe injury that kept him out for weeks. Once again, Swift fumbled and didn't see another snap the rest of the day. He finished the game with 13 carries for 51 yards, along with two catches for eight yards, and a receiving touchdown.

Not only are Swift's fumbles hurting the team's scoring chances, but they're forcing Johnson to use alternative players while he rides the bench. That could prove to be problematic if injuries keep piling up, or it causes overuse like it did with Monangai. The fumbles are one thing; the trust is another. Swift must get this under control before better organizations can take advantage of his mistakes.

Across the season, the shortlisted athletes and teams featured in major events, national and international competitions, and important milestones in their respective disciplines. Srikanth’s performances showcased his enduring competitiveness and value to Indian badminton.AYUSH SHETTYAge: 21Key Achievements in 2026:- Won silver at the Badminton Asia Championships- Defeated defending world champion and world No. 1 Shi Yuqi at the BWF World Championships- Helped India secure bronze in the Thomas Cup in Horsens, Denmark- Contributed to India’s bronze-medal finish in the men’s team event at the 20th Asian Games in Aichi-NagoyaAyush Shetty enjoyed a breakthrough 2026 season, emerging as one of the brightest prospects in Indian men’s singles badminton and climbing to a career-high world ranking of No. 18. He grabbed global attention at the BWF World Championships in New Delhi, stunning defending champion and world No. 1 Shi Yuqi 21-14, 13-21, 21-19 in the opening round to end the top seed’s title defence. Shetty advanced to the Round of 16 before exiting against Indonesia’s Alwi Farhan. articles.title: ‘A chance to get home:’ Mark Turgeon looks to build a winner at Kansas City
articles.summary: NEW ROCHELLE, N.Y. — Mark Turgeon wasn’t bored. The former Texas A&M and Maryland head coach was enjoying his retirement, which lasted four and a half years...
articles.body:
NEW ROCHELLE, N.Y. — Mark Turgeon wasn't bored.

The former Texas A&M and Maryland head coach was enjoying his retirement, which lasted four and a half years after his firing from the Terps in December 2021, but when the Kansas City job opened, he felt that he had a chance to do something special.

"It was a chance to get home," said Turgeon, a Topeka, Kan., native who played at KU. "I'm excited to be back in it with my son (assistant coach Will Turgeon). I've got a great staff, guys I believe in. I got a great athletic director, and I'm in a great city."

It certainly, though, seemed odd at the time. Turgeon is 61 years old and hasn't coached at the mid-major level in nearly two decades. He was at the helm of two high-major programs for a combined 14 years.

Turgeon has won over 475 games as a college basketball coach, has won NCAA Tournament games at three different schools, and taken two programs to the Sweet 16. That's what makes it so jarring to see him now standing on the sideline wearing the Summit League on his shoulder as his Kansas City Roos lost 62-61 in a road game at Iona on Friday.

But he has an appreciation for what the mid-major game still is to this day.

"That's why I chose this level," Turgeon said. "So I don't have to get into the million dollars and all that kind of stuff."

He still has to raise money for his roster, but he's not spending seven figures on players the way the he would have if he found a gig – as head coach or assistant – at a higher level. He's gotten financial support for his program from people he knows in the Kansas City community, but he's not all that worried about the money.

However, it's a pretty big lifestyle adjustment.

"What sucks is all the road games," Turgeon said. "If you count our exhibition games, we've had seven of our first 10 games on the road. Jeez, I'm tired. I'm too old for that, right? So that's the biggest thing at this level. Scheduling is impossible. Our league only plays 14 league games, so we have 18 non-conference (games). So, almost every game we play, the (opponent) has more time to prepare than we do."

"I was used to Maryland and A&M and even Wichita State, buying games and winning games, and being 11-2 at the Christmas break, enjoying Christmas and all that kind of stuff," Turgeon continued.

The Roos won just one Division-I game last season, and the program went 5-27 in Summit League play over the last two seasons. Turgeon's hire was announced in February, allowing him to get a very early start in recruiting and fundraising, and he's built a roster that is a clear step up from the last group.

Kansas City played Creighton close on night one of the season, then beat Southern Illinois at home, scoring 100 points. The team is 3-4 and was one layup against Iona away from being 4-3. San Diego transfer Assane Diop has been excellent on the glass. ETSU transfer guard Jaylen Smith struggled against Iona, but has the makings of an excellent Summit League lead guard. There are local freshmen Lincoln Goodwin and Cameron Love, who can both make an impact.

Turgeon blamed himself for a poor performance against Division-II Newman and thinks that despite the loss, the Roos took steps forward against Iona. He said the Gaels are one of the most athletic teams that Kansas City will face all year, and they won the battle on the glass.

"We got better because I'm figuring out how to coach them," he said. "And once we start making all those open shots that we missed, we're going to be really hard to guard."

This probably isn't a Summit League contender in year one, but it's a team that Turgeon believes will set the tone for future groups.

"I imagine year two will be a lot better than we are in year one," Turgeon said. "And I think we're going to be pretty good in year one."

Turgeon thinks this will be his last job. "Nights like tonight kill you," he said after the loss to Iona, faced with some of the more difficult emotions of being back in the game. But even then, he says that being at home near his family makes him feel less nervous on a game-by-game basis.

He's confident in what he's building long-term.

Over the first nine months in the job, Turgeon has helped raise the money to "fix up" the Kansas City athletics offices and his team's locker room. That's all part of the process to building a winner.

"I've won everywhere," Turgeon said. "I'm not concerned about winning here. I think we're going to win at a high level. It's going to take time. I'm probably going to build a really great program and hand it off to somebody else because I don't know how long I'll do this."

articles.title: Arteta provides encouraging update on Raya injury

articles.body:
Mikel Arteta has confirmed David Raya will miss Arsenal's Champions League clash with Borussia Dortmund but says the goalkeeper's injury is not as serious as initially feared.

Raya was forced off during Saturday's 2-2 draw with Newcastle after suffering an arm injury, prompting concerns he could be set for a long spell out.

But Arteta delivered a more encouraging update ahead of Tuesday's meeting with Dortmund at the Emirates Stadium.

"Yeah, he's not fit for tomorrow unfortunately, but it doesn't look too serious," the Arsenal boss said.

"We need some more tests tomorrow, but it's quite encouraging.

"With the pain that he was showing immediately after the action, we were all quite worried, but he seems to be better than what we expected."

articles.title: 49ers’ Mike Evans Makes Feelings Clear on Brock Purdy After Vikings Win
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers dismantled the Minnesota Vikings 35-10 on Sunday night in Mexico City. No team had scored more than 23 against Minnesota’s defense al...
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers dismantled the Minnesota Vikings 35-10 on Sunday night in Mexico City. No team had scored more than 23 against Minnesota's defense all season. The 49ers put up 28 before halftime.

Brock Purdy was surgical, connecting on 21 of his 26 attempts for 255 yards with three touchdown throws. He was sacked just once against the most blitz-heavy defense in football. George Kittle caught two of those touchdowns. The crowd at Estadio Banorte was overwhelmingly pro-San Francisco, and it felt like a home game from the opening drive.

But the return of one player changed the complexion of the night. And after the game, he made clear exactly what he thinks about the quarterback throwing him the ball.

Mike Evans missed three games with Achilles tendinitis. In his first game back for the 49ers, he hauled in six receptions for 109 yards and a score. The majority of his production came before halftime, with 91 yards in the opening two quarters. The Vikings had no answer for his route combinations against their blitz packages.

After the game, Evans was asked about Purdy. His response left nothing to interpretation.

"Man, he's the best player in the game right now," Evans said . "He's super dialed in. The way he prepares. The way he competes. He's tough. I always thought he's been underrated. His precision. Super smart player."

Evans also spoke about how it felt to be back on the field for the 49ers in an atmosphere unlike anything he had experienced.

"I feel amazing," Evans said. "This is one of the best atmospheres I've been a part of. Shout out to the Mexico fans."

Purdy did not just survive against Brian Flores' defense. He attacked it. Purdy opened the game by completing his first eight passes for 135 yards and a pair of scores. He went 16-for-18 when facing Minnesota's blitz, posting 195 yards and a 148.8 passer rating according to Next Gen Stats.

Head coach Kyle Shanahan gave the game ball to Purdy.

"Our quarterback was unbelievable," Shanahan said. "You can't hesitate versus those guys. You got to let it rip. And he continually did that over and over while protecting the ball."

The 49ers also put together a 98-yard touchdown drive in the third quarter that consumed over seven minutes and effectively ended the game. Keenan Allen came up with a pair of third-down conversions. Deebo Samuel broke free for 20 yards on a reverse. The drive was a statement from an offense operating at full capacity for the first time this season.

The 49ers are 9-1. Purdy is playing at an MVP level. And the player with the longest resume on the roster just told everyone what the rest of the league is starting to figure out. Purdy is among the best in the game right now.

articles.title: ‘I want to lose this game’: Dave Portnoy is rooting against Michigan in Ohio State rivalry game
articles.summary: The Michigan Wolverines will head to Columbus to take on the Ohio State Buckeyes on Saturday, with both programs coming off disappointing seasons and both he...
articles.body:
The Michigan Wolverines will head to Columbus to take on the Ohio State Buckeyes on Saturday, with both programs coming off disappointing seasons and both head coaches facing serious questions about their futures. Michigan is just 6-5, while Ohio State has dropped three of its last four games to fall to 7-4.

Barstool Sports founder Dave Portnoy, one of Michigan's most famous fans, has already made it clear that he isn't a fan of either coach. Now, he's taking things a step further, saying that he wants the Wolverines to lose to their biggest rival so that Michigan will move on from Kyle Whittingham.

Michigan hired Whittingham away from Utah last December after firing Sherrone Moore. But his first season in Ann Arbor hasn't gone according to plan. The Wolverines lost home games to Iowa, Indiana, and Michigan State, along with road losses to Minnesota and Oregon. The Michigan State loss led Portnoy to say that Whittingham was "asleep at the wheel."

Michigan did pull off a stunning 18-16 triple-overtime upset of previously unbeaten No. 4 UCLA on Saturday to become bowl eligible, but that hardly saved their season.

Things have gone even worse in Columbus over the past month. Ohio State started 6-1, but has since lost to USC, Oregon, and Nebraska, and the criticism of Ryan Day has never been louder.

After Ohio State's loss to Nebraska on Saturday, Portnoy took to X to call this year's matchup the "worst big game in the history of the rivalry," and said that both fanbases need an embarrassing loss to fire their coaches.

Portnoy doubled down on Monday's episode of Wake Up Barstool , going as far as saying that he's rooting against his own team. He also suggested that Michigan should give the job to defensive coordinator Jay Hill.

"It's gonna be the worst big game I think since 1960 or something like that. Both teams are eliminated. Both teams hate their coach. You want to give Jay Hill the job, give Jay Hill the job. People are going to say this, that I'm not a Michigan man, I'm not a real Michigan man because I want them to lose this week against Ohio State. But I do. I don't want them to win this game," Portnoy said on Monday morning via X .

Portnoy said that a win over the Buckeyes wouldn't mean much this year, saying there's "nothing on the line."

"There's nothing on the line in this game except pride. It's a new era. The importance of this game, it's you beat your opponent, you have a great season because you ruin theirs. There's nothing on the line here. There's not," Portnoy said.

He then took aim at Whittingham directly, referencing the stadium in Utah where Whittingham spent the previous 21 seasons as head coach.

"Michigan could have beat Indiana at home, should have beat Iowa. They just did this. It's a disgusting season. And I'm convinced Whittingham, who thinks he's playing in Rice-Eccles Stadium still, isn't the guy. So I want him gone, and I want to lose this game. If that doesn't make me a Michigan man, then you're not a Michigan man," Portnoy said.

Portnoy added that he isn't going to gloat if the Wolverines lose, and that he was "not happy about the UCLA game at all."

It's certainly odd for someone to be rooting against their own team in the most heated rivalry in all of college football, but that's where Portnoy's at right now.

articles.title: ¡15-0! Spain fall one goal short of U17 World Cup record 🔥
articles.summary: Spain’s Under-17 team produced an unprecedented attacking display as they crushed Fiji 15-0 at the Under-17 World Cup. The national side delivered a memorabl...
articles.body:
Spain's Under-17 team produced an unprecedented attacking display as they crushed Fiji 15-0 at the Under-17 World Cup. The national side delivered a memorable performance that left them just one goal short of equalling the biggest win in the tournament's history.

Spain dominated from the opening whistle. Rafa Cruz opened the scoring in the fifth minute and led the attack with five goals (5', 10', 21', 57' and 65'). Roberto Tomás (12', 19' and 35') and Guillermo Trujillano (25', 40' and 51') joined the scoring spree with a hat-trick apiece, putting the game beyond doubt before half-time.

Spain's hunger for goals did not diminish in the second half. Marco Company (43'), a brace from defender Jorge Domínguez (54' and 74') and a final goal from Yeremaiah Santos in the 80th minute completed the rout against a totally outclassed Fiji side.

This emphatic 15-0 victory leaves Spain just short of the World Cup's all-time record. That mark still belongs to Morocco, who previously beat New Caledonia 16-0.

Despite falling one goal short of the historic record, the team have sent a powerful warning to the other sides at the Under-17 World Cup, showcasing devastating finishing and outstanding form.

articles.summary: Boxer Lauren Price excited by stadium fight plans.
articles.body:
Lauren Price says she is "excited" by the prospect of a stadium fight in Cardiff after becoming the undisputed world welterweight champion.

The Welsh boxer, 32, added the WBO title to her collection and become the first Welsh fighter to hold all four major world titles when she beat Michaela Kotaskova at Cardiff's Utilita Arena.

Price told BBC Radio Wales Breakfast that she wants to bring "massive" nights back to the Welsh capital.

articles.title: ‘I’m ready to upset the odds’: Josh Kelly confident he wins unification match with Boots Ennis
articles.summary: Josh Kelly says he’ll be fighting in a flow state against Boots Ennis.
articles.body:
IBF champion Josh Kelly spends some time talking about his upcoming super welterweight title unification match with WBO champion Jaron 'Boots' Ennis scheduled for Feb. 27 in Atlanta. Although Kelly will come into this fight expected to lose, he explains that he has all of the pressure off of him and that he's looking forward to upsetting the odds by beating Boots to become unified champion. Here's some of what he had to say below.

Kelly on how he looks at his upcoming matchup against Boots

"I think this fight you're going to have to adjust round to round, minute to minute, even seconds — you're going to have to keep adjusting your style. So it's whoever can adjust first is going to get the better of the fight and end up coming out on top. But I wholeheartedly believe in myself and I wouldn't be sat right here taking on a test like this if I didn't.

"I'm running into the fire, I want to test myself and I believe in myself…I'm not the guy that shows out the most but when I'm in fight night and when I'm in that competitive mindset, there's no guy that's coming close to me when I'm in my flow."

On coming into this fight being the underdog

"I love having the odds stacked against me. It just let's me be free, let's me go in there and do me and I'm dangerous when I'm like that."

On what he takes from Boots fight against Zayas

"There's a few things but I'm not going to let them out now. I'll keep that for fight night, I'm going to keep them all under wraps, but yeah, there's a few things [I can take advantage of]. Don't worry about that."

On what he thinks the key is to winning the fight

"For me, just staying in my flow and being clever. I think mindset and flow [are the keys].

"I surprise a lot of people when I'm in front of them. They don't think I'm that fast, they don't think I hit as hard as I do. And listen, it's their downfall. I love people sleeping on me but I don't think him and his dad are because like his dad said, once before they faced me. I was only a baby then so I have matured into the guy I am now, 32. And I'm ready to upset the odds."

On his intentions to pursue a Fundora fight if he beats Boots

"It's Boots, Fundora and then sail off into the sunset. I don't need to do much after that. I'm alright. Them are the two fights that I predict I'm going to get, I'm going to win, and legacy stamped in, name stamped in history."

articles.title: 3 biggest risers in NHL after Week 8
articles.summary: The NHL season heads into Week 9 and these are the biggest risers around the league.
articles.body:
Another week of the 2026 NHL season has wrapped up, and there have been plenty of good things to talk about. Goaltending has been a struggle in the entire league, and not many teams have a goalie they can rely on. Offense wins games when their top players perform, and New York might have an under-the-radar star in the making. Here are the risers after Week 9.

The Dallas Stars are playing some great hockey right now. Mikko Rantanen is playing at a point-per-game rate. Their offense is their heartbeat. Jason Robertson, Roope Hintz, and Wyatt Johnson are their core, and it is a very solid core. Dallas is playing good hockey right now, and they should keep it up.

Linus Ullmark has been one of the main reasons why the Senators are playing like an elite team right now. Getting good goaltending right now in the NHL feels weird because of how down the overall save percentage is in the game. But Ullmark is making this league look easy. The Senators are at the top of their division, and one of the key reasons is because of their goalie.

Many would think Bo Horvat would be the team's leading scorer without Mat Barzal, but if one player has played a major role in the New York Islanders' success, it is Simon Holmstrom. 10 goals so far this season. He is currently on pace for 38 goals this year, which would be a career year for him. He had 19 goals last season, and in just 22 games, he has 10. An under-the-radar player that not many people are talking about for the Isles.

articles.title: Kenneth Walker and Emmett Johnson could do what no Kansas City Chiefs pair have managed since 2010
articles.summary: Kansas City Chiefs running backs Kenneth Walker and Emmett Johnson could manage a rare feat. Emmett Johnson’s emergence has been the unexpected bonus for the...
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs running backs Kenneth Walker and Emmett Johnson could manage a rare feat.

Emmett Johnson's emergence has been the unexpected bonus for the Kansas City Chiefs' season. The fifth-round pick is demonstrating that he is a starting-level caliber player.

Johnson is valuable insurance for big free agent signing Kenneth Walker, who had an incredible start to the season.

Despite missing the past two games, Kenneth Walker has totalled 1,044 scrimmage yards already this season.

Walker's 1,044 yards are broken down by 872 rushing yards and 172 receiving.

Emmett Johnson is not far behind. He already has 662 yards, 317 rushing and 347 receiving.

Walker and Johnson could both surpass 1,000 yards: First Chiefs pair in 16 years

If Emmett Johnson can reach 1,000 total scrimmage yards and to follow Kenneth Walker, it will represent a rare achievement.

The last time the Kansas City Chiefs had two running backs surpassing 1,000 scrimmage yards in the same season was 2010.

Jamaal Charles' incredible 1,935 yards was followed by Thomas Jones with 1,018 yards.

Kenneth Walker is expected to return from injury in Week 12, and while this will slash Johnson's opportunity, he has earned the right to play a big role in the offense.

The Chiefs have seven games remaining of the regular season, and Johnson needs 338 yards.

This breaks down to only 48.3 yards per game, a very achievable number.

It must be noted that the Chiefs play an extra game in 2026 than the players did in 2010. While this won't minimise the achievement – it would be even more impressive if Johnson can surpass 1,000 ahead of Week 18 against the Las Vegas Raiders.

articles.title: Vote for the Register Athlete of the Week for Nov. 15-21
articles.summary: Here are the Register's Athlete of the Week candidates from the metro area for the week of Nov. 15-21.
articles.body:
The week of Nov. 15-21 saw the Iowa high school football state championship games take place at the UNI-Dome in Cedar Falls.

Dowling Catholic was crowned the 5A state champion for the 12th time in program history with a 31-24 victory over Johnston; Cedar Rapids Xavier crushed Sergeant Bluff-Luton 56-6 in 4A, and Solon cruised to a 27-7 victory over Des Moines Christian in 3A. In 2A, Central Lyon/George-Little Rock won a 13-7 defensive battle over Spirit Lake; Regina rolled to a 49-3 victory over Aplington-Parkersburg in 1A, Woodbury Central downed West Sioux, 35-13, in Class A and Woodbine won the 8-player title with a 36-28 win over Gladbrook-Reinbeck.

There were several impressive individual performances by high school football players and girls wrestlers and basketball players from the Des Moines metro area during the week.

Here are the Des Moines Register's Athlete of the Week candidates from the Des Moines metro area for the week of Nov. 15-21. DesMoinesRegister.com readers vote to determine the winners, who will be announced at the end of the week.

La Cava turned in a masterful performance at quarterback to lead Dowling Catholic past Johnston, 31-24, in the Class 5A championship game of the Iowa high school football playoffs on Nov. 21 at the UNI-Dome in Cedar Falls.

La Cava completed 14 of 19 passes for 159 yards and two touchdowns with no interceptions. He also had a breakout game running the football, picking 134 yards and one touchdown on just 10 carries.

Helming had a gutsy effort in defeat for the Johnston football team during its 31-24 loss to Dowling Catholic in the 5A state championship game on Nov. 21 at the UNI-Dome in Cedar Falls.

Helming completed 22 of 29 passes for 250 yards and one touchdown with no interceptions. He also ran for a touchdown.

Newton accounted for Des Moines Christian's only touchdown during its 27-7 loss to Solon in the 3A football state championship game on Nov. 20 at the UNI-Dome in Cedar Falls.

Newton delivered the Lion touchdown on special teams during the first quarter. He returned a kickoff 79 yards to the house.

Van Beek placed first at 100 pounds during the Central Iowa Kickoff girls wrestling tournament on Nov. 21 at Nevada.

Van Beek pinned Ankeny's Elsa Sullivan in the quarterfinals, and she upset top seed Livia Smith of South Tama in the semifinals with a win by fall. In the finals, Van Beek defeated Ogden's Rylin Casey by a 3-0 decision.

Bratland placed first at 145 pounds during the Central Iowa Kickoff girls wrestling tournament on Nov. 21 in Nevada.

Bratland pinned Algona's Emmy Owen in 1:07 during the finals to cap a 4-0 day that saw her record three falls and one technical fall.

articles.title: Caleb Williams and Bears' offense struggle in ugly win
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears are now 8-2 but it is clear Caleb Williams and their offense need to step it up the next few weeks
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears returned from their off week with a performance very similar to their game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The Bears got their eighth victory of the season, but they didn't reinforce the idea that this team is ready to take the NFC. The positive elements of this game were offset by some negative developments that will create concern heading into a tough stretch of games.

Following his four-interception game against the Bucs, Caleb Williams looked very hesitant against the New Orleans Saints . Caleb finished the game 15-23, with 181 yards, 2 touchdowns and an interception. This is not the game many people wanted to see from him following an off week.

The Bears' offense has not been the reason they have won football games the last two weeks. That is a completely different storyline from the majority of this season. Caleb and the offense struggled mightily on the ground and through the air. They were good enough to get the job done, but more credit in this game has to go to the Bears' defense.

Jeffery Simmons led the way with 3 sacks, and the Bears had 6 sacks overall. Jeffery Simmons was the best player on the entire field. A game like this really shows that the trade was more than worth it. While the Bears offense struggled, the Saints offense was the worst unit on the field. That was directly due to how good the Bears defense was.

It is encouraging to see the Bears defense can win football games for the team, but moving forward, as things get tougher, the Bears will need both sides of the ball to play well. Caleb Williams and the Bears offense will get a great opportunity on Thanksgiving against the Detroit Lions to show what they are capable of.
